text: server accepts non-ASCII digits in a price; both clients reject them

Done in 7db8395. Fixed in all three copies rather than just the broken one: the two clients were already ASCII-only so those edits are runtime no-ops, but the failure mode WAS that the patterns look identical, so relying on each language's default is what let them diverge unnoticed. A test asserts the pattern is ASCII by construction ([0-9] present, \\d absent), so reintroducing \\d fails immediately. Sweep result: the server has exactly three regexes and only this one used \\d; CURRENCY_RE is an explicit ASCII range and agrees everywhere. Found but deliberately not fixed here: EMAIL_RE's \\s has the same cross-language asymmetry, but runs the SAFE way round (server stricter than clients), so it is a UX inconsistency rather than a data-integrity hole.
